ok.balance: The arm is level. The crane lifts.
ok.flow: Every tank is on its line.
ok.routing: Every parcel is in its bin.
ok.gears: The hand lands on its mark.
fail.balance.unplaced: A crate is still on the ground.
fail.balance.tips_left: The arm drops on the left.
fail.balance.tips_right: The arm drops on the right.
fail.ray.too_direct: The beam needs more bounces first.
fail.shadow.off_left: The shadow falls too far left.
fail.shadow.off_right: The shadow falls too far right.
fail.flow.too_low: A tank stops short of its line.
fail.flow.too_high: A tank rises past its line.
fail.routing.misplaced: Some parcels land in the wrong bin.
fail.locks.jammed: The lock stays shut. A dial is off its mark.
fail.gears.missing_gear: A peg is empty, so the hand never moves.
fail.cargo.left_behind: A crate is still on the dock.
fail.cargo.lists_left: The ship leans to the left.
fail.cargo.lists_right: The ship leans to the right.
scene.balance.a.objective: Hang the loose crate so the arm stays level.
scene.balance.a.reveal: You found the one hook where a single crate holds the arm level against the other.
scene.balance.b.objective: Hang every crate so the arm stays level.
scene.balance.b.reveal: You spread several crates so that their pulls on each side added up the same.
scene.balance.c.objective: Some hooks are broken. Hang every crate and keep the arm level.
scene.balance.c.reveal: With fewer hooks to choose from, you still found the places that cancel out.
scene.ray.a.objective: Turn the mirror so the beam reaches the sensor.
scene.ray.a.reveal: You tilted the mirror until the beam left it straight toward the sensor.
scene.ray.b.objective: Turn the mirrors so the beam reaches the sensor.
scene.ray.b.reveal: You lined up one bounce after another until the beam arrived.
scene.ray.c.objective: Walls are in the way. Bounce the beam around them to the sensor.
scene.ray.c.reveal: You steered the beam around the walls using nothing but the tilt of each mirror.
scene.shadow.a.objective: Slide the lamp so the shadow covers the painted patch.
scene.shadow.a.reveal: You moved the lamp until the board's shadow landed on the patch.
scene.shadow.b.objective: Slide and raise the lamp so the shadow covers the patch exactly.
scene.shadow.b.reveal: You set the lamp's height for the right size and its position for the right spot.
scene.shadow.c.objective: Move the lamp and the board so the shadow covers the patch exactly.
scene.shadow.c.reveal: You juggled three things at once and still made the shadow fit.
scene.flow.a.objective: Set the taps so every tank fills to its line.
scene.flow.a.reveal: You opened each tap just enough for the water to stop on the line.
scene.flow.b.objective: The tanks have different widths. Set the taps so each one fills to its line.
scene.flow.b.reveal: You gave the wide tanks more water so they rose as far as they needed.
scene.flow.c.objective: Set the taps and the timer so every tank fills to its line.
scene.flow.c.reveal: You balanced the taps and the time so every tank finished on its line together.
scene.routing.a.objective: Set the junctions so every parcel lands in the bin of its colour.
scene.routing.a.reveal: You set each junction so that every parcel found its own bin.
scene.routing.b.objective: Three colours now. Set the junctions so every parcel lands in its own bin.
scene.routing.b.reveal: You chose which colour each junction pulls aside, and the rest followed.
scene.routing.c.objective: Some junctions flip after every parcel. Set them all so each parcel lands in its own bin.
scene.routing.c.reveal: You planned for junctions that change as they go, and it still came out sorted.
scene.locks.a.objective: Turn the dials until each one points at its mark, then open the lock.
scene.locks.a.reveal: You found the turns that brought both dials to their marks.
scene.locks.b.objective: Three linked dials. Bring each one to its mark, then open the lock.
scene.locks.b.reveal: You worked out which dial drags which, and turned them in an order that works.
scene.locks.c.objective: Every dial pulls on others. Bring them all to their marks, then open the lock.
scene.locks.c.reveal: You combined turns that undo each other's side effects until every dial sat on its mark.
scene.gears.a.objective: Fit a gear so the hand goes round exactly {turns}× while the crank goes round {crank}×.
scene.gears.a.reveal: You picked the gear whose size makes the hand keep pace exactly.
scene.gears.b.objective: Fit the gears so the hand goes round exactly {turns}× while the crank goes round {crank}×.
scene.gears.b.reveal: You chose gears whose sizes together give exactly the right speed.
scene.gears.c.objective: Fit every gear so the hand goes round exactly {turns}× while the crank goes round {crank}×.
scene.gears.c.reveal: You built a chain of gears that, step by step, reaches the exact speed.
scene.cargo.a.objective: Load every crate into the hold.
scene.cargo.a.reveal: You turned and placed the crates until they filled the hold with no gaps.
scene.cargo.b.objective: Load every crate and keep the ship level. Dotted crates are heavy.
scene.cargo.b.reveal: You filled the hold and kept the heavy crates balanced across the middle.
scene.cargo.c.objective: Part of the hold is blocked. Load every crate and keep the ship level.
scene.cargo.c.reveal: You fitted everything around the blocked space and still kept the ship level.
hint.balance.a.1: A crate pulls harder the farther out it hangs.
hint.balance.a.2: A light crate far out can match a heavy crate close in.
hint.balance.a.3: Count the hooks from the middle on each side. Heavy and near can equal light and far.
hint.balance.b.1: Every crate adds its own pull. The two sides only need the same total.
hint.balance.b.2: Try the heaviest crate first, close to the middle. Then adjust with the light ones.
hint.balance.b.3: For each crate, think of its weight and its hooks from the middle together. Make the two sides add up equal.
hint.balance.c.1: Broken hooks can't be used. Look at what is left on each side first.
hint.balance.c.2: Work out how much pull one side still needs. Then see which crate and hook give exactly that.
hint.balance.c.3: If nothing fits, swap two crates. A small move far out changes more than a big move near the middle.
hint.ray.a.1: The beam leaves a mirror at the same slant it arrived.
hint.ray.a.2: Turn the mirror a little and watch which way the beam swings.
hint.ray.a.3: Face the mirror halfway between where the beam comes from and where it must go.
hint.ray.b.1: Sort out the first mirror the beam meets before touching the next.
hint.ray.b.2: Each mirror only has to send the beam on to the next one.
hint.ray.b.3: Work backwards. Which mirror can see the sensor? Aim the beam at that mirror first.
hint.ray.c.1: Walls stop the beam. Mirrors are the only way around them.
hint.ray.c.2: Find a clear line into the sensor, then get the beam onto that line.
hint.ray.c.3: Check if the beam can bounce twice before it reaches the sensor. The long way round may be the only open one.
hint.shadow.a.1: Move the lamp one way and the shadow slides the other way.
hint.shadow.a.2: The shadow always falls on the far side of the board from the lamp.
hint.shadow.a.3: Imagine a straight string from the lamp past each edge of the board. Where the strings touch the ground is where the shadow ends.
hint.shadow.b.1: A low lamp throws a long shadow. A high lamp throws a short one.
hint.shadow.b.2: Get the shadow the right width first by raising or lowering the lamp. Then slide it into place.
hint.shadow.b.3: When the lamp hangs twice as high as the board, the shadow is twice as wide as the board.
hint.shadow.c.1: The lamp's height sets how much bigger the shadow is than the board.
hint.shadow.c.2: Fix the size with the lamp's height. Then use the board and the lamp's position to place the shadow.
hint.shadow.c.3: Sliding the board moves the shadow the same way. Sliding the lamp moves it the opposite way.
hint.flow.a.1: A wider-open tap fills its tank faster.
hint.flow.a.2: The timer runs the same for every tank. Only the taps differ.
hint.flow.a.3: Run it once and see how far the water gets. Opening the tap twice as far gives twice the height.
hint.flow.b.1: A wide tank needs more water to rise the same height.
hint.flow.b.2: A tank twice as wide rises half as fast from the same tap.
hint.flow.b.3: For each tank, look at its width and its line. A wide tank with a high line needs the most open tap.
hint.flow.c.1: A longer timer raises every tank. The taps set how the tanks differ from each other.
hint.flow.c.2: First use the taps to get the tanks right compared with each other. Then use the timer to lift them all.
hint.flow.c.3: If the pump is weak, opening everything wide makes every tap weaker. Open only what you need.
hint.routing.a.1: Follow one parcel with your finger from the top to see where it ends up.
hint.routing.a.2: A plain junction sends everything the same way. A colour junction pulls one colour aside.
hint.routing.a.3: Start at the bins. For each bin, which way must the junction above it send that colour?
hint.routing.b.1: A colour junction sends its own colour left and all the others right.
hint.routing.b.2: Decide which colour must leave the line first, and set the top junction to it.
hint.routing.b.3: Once one colour is pulled aside, the junctions below only have to deal with what is left.
hint.routing.c.1: A flipping junction sends one parcel left, the next one right, then left again.
hint.routing.c.2: Look at the order the parcels arrive in. A flip only matters for the parcels that reach it.
hint.routing.c.3: Count which parcels reach a flipping junction, in order. Set its first side so that the first of them goes the right way.
hint.locks.a.1: Turning one dial drags the other along. Watch which one follows.
hint.locks.a.2: Set the dial that moves others first. Finish with the one that moves alone.
hint.locks.a.3: A dial that goes all the way round ends where it began. One click back is the same as going forward almost a full circle.
hint.locks.b.1: Turn each dial once and notice which others move with it.
hint.locks.b.2: Find a dial that moves only itself. Leave that one for last.
hint.locks.b.3: Fix the dials in order. Start with the one nothing else can correct later, and end with the one that turns alone.
hint.locks.c.1: Some dials turn others backwards. Check the direction, not only which ones move.
hint.locks.c.2: The order of your turns does not change where the dials end up. Only how many times you turn each one matters.
hint.locks.c.3: Pick one dial and bring it to its mark. Then use dials that don't disturb it to fix the rest.
hint.gears.a.1: A small gear pushed by a big one spins faster.
hint.gears.a.2: Count the teeth. A gear with half the teeth turns twice as often.
hint.gears.a.3: Compare the teeth of the two gears that touch. If one has three times the teeth, the other turns three times as often.
hint.gears.b.1: It is the pair that matters: the gear that pushes and the gear being pushed.
hint.gears.b.2: To speed the hand up, let a big gear push a small one. To slow it down, do the opposite.
hint.gears.b.3: Two pairs in a row build on each other. Doubling the speed twice gives four times the speed.
hint.gears.c.1: First judge roughly how much faster or slower the hand must go than the crank.
hint.gears.c.2: Split the job between the pairs. One pair can do most of it and the other the rest.
hint.gears.c.3: For each pair, compare the pusher's teeth with the pushed gear's teeth. All the pairs together must give the hand's turns compared with the crank's turns.
hint.cargo.a.1: Tap a crate to turn it. Long crates often fit better the other way.
hint.cargo.a.2: Place the biggest crates first. The small ones fill what is left.
hint.cargo.a.3: Count the squares. The crates cover the hold exactly, so any gap means something must move.
hint.cargo.b.1: Heavy crates near one side make the ship lean that way.
hint.cargo.b.2: Put heavy crates near the middle, or one on each side at the same distance.
hint.cargo.b.3: How hard a crate tips the ship depends on its weight and how far it sits from the middle. Make the left and right add up the same.
hint.cargo.c.1: Blocked squares can't hold crates. Fit the awkward corners first.
hint.cargo.c.2: Get every crate aboard first. Then swap crates of the same shape to fix the lean.
hint.cargo.c.3: Swapping a heavy crate with a light one of the same size keeps the fit and changes the balance.
concept.balance_a.name: The law of the lever
concept.balance_a.idea: Weight times distance from the pivot was the same on both sides. That product is called a moment.
concept.balance_b.name: Adding moments
concept.balance_b.idea: Each crate adds its weight times its distance to its side. The arm is level when the two sums match.
concept.balance_b.seen: Loading an aeroplane, a hanging mobile, kitchen scales
concept.balance_c.name: Solving for the unknown
concept.balance_c.idea: You had a total to reach and limited choices, and found the values that make both sides equal. That is solving an equation.
concept.balance_c.seen: Balancing a budget, adjusting a recipe, trimming a boat
concept.ray_a.name: The law of reflection
concept.ray_a.idea: Light bounces off a flat mirror at the same angle it hits it.
concept.ray_a.seen: Rear-view mirrors, periscopes, a ball off a cushion
concept.ray_b.name: Chained reflections
concept.ray_b.idea: Every bounce follows the same rule, so a whole path can be built one angle at a time.
concept.ray_b.seen: Kaleidoscopes, laser shows, trick shots in pool
concept.ray_c.name: Paths made of angles
concept.ray_c.idea: By choosing the angle at each mirror you planned a route around obstacles. Geometry did the steering.
concept.ray_c.seen: Fibre-optic cables, sound in a concert hall, radar
concept.shadow_a.name: Projection
concept.shadow_a.idea: Light travels in straight lines, so a shadow is the board's outline carried along those lines to the ground.
concept.shadow_b.name: Similar triangles
concept.shadow_b.idea: The lamp, the board and its shadow make two triangles of the same shape. Their sizes stay in step, so the lamp's height sets the shadow's width.
concept.shadow_b.seen: Measuring a tree by its shadow, zooming a projector, long evening shadows
concept.shadow_c.name: Scale and proportion
concept.shadow_c.idea: The shadow is the board enlarged by a fixed ratio set by the two heights. Change the ratio and every length changes together.
concept.shadow_c.seen: Maps and plans, enlarging a photo, a torch held near a wall
concept.flow_a.name: Rate and time
concept.flow_a.idea: How much you get is how fast it flows multiplied by how long it runs.
concept.flow_a.seen: Filling a bucket, charging a phone, driving at a steady speed
concept.flow_b.name: Volume and height
concept.flow_b.idea: The water's volume is the tank's base times its height, so the same volume stands lower in a wider tank.
concept.flow_b.seen: Pouring a drink into a wide glass, filling a bath, rain gauges
concept.flow_c.name: Sharing a fixed supply
concept.flow_c.idea: There was only so much flow to go round. You split it in the right proportions and chose the time to match.
concept.flow_c.seen: Water pressure when two taps run, sharing a budget, splitting an internet connection
concept.routing_a.name: Decision trees
concept.routing_a.idea: Each junction is a yes-or-no question. A chain of them can sort anything into the right place.
concept.routing_a.seen: Sorting the post, a quiz flowchart, the game of twenty questions
concept.routing_b.name: Sorting by rules
concept.routing_b.idea: If it is this colour, go left; otherwise carry on. Simple rules in the right order sort a whole mixture.
concept.routing_b.seen: Recycling plants, email filters, coin sorters
concept.routing_c.name: Machines with memory
concept.routing_c.idea: A flipping junction remembers what it did last. Systems whose next move depends on their past are called state machines.
concept.routing_c.seen: Traffic lights, turnstiles, a light switch
concept.locks_a.name: Clock arithmetic
concept.locks_a.idea: On a dial, counting wraps around: past the last position you are back at the first. This is called modular arithmetic.
concept.locks_a.seen: Clock faces, days of the week, combination locks
concept.locks_b.name: Linked equations
concept.locks_b.idea: Each turn changed several dials at once. Finding how many turns of each one gives the right totals is solving several equations together.
concept.locks_b.seen: Mixing paint colours, a twisting cube puzzle, adjusting a recipe
concept.locks_c.name: Combining moves
concept.locks_c.idea: Turns add up the same in any order, so you could treat each dial's turns as a number and find the mix that lands every dial at once.
concept.locks_c.seen: Puzzle boxes, sliders on a sound mixer, tuning a guitar
concept.gears_a.name: Ratios
concept.gears_a.idea: Two meshed gears turn in the ratio of their teeth, flipped over: fewer teeth means more turns.
concept.gears_a.seen: Bicycle gears, hand whisks, clockwork toys
concept.gears_b.name: Multiplying ratios
concept.gears_b.idea: Each pair of gears multiplies the speed by its own ratio, and pairs in a row multiply together.
concept.gears_b.seen: Car gearboxes, wind-up clocks, drill speeds
concept.gears_c.name: Gear trains
concept.gears_c.idea: A long chain of gears is several ratios multiplied together. Choosing them means breaking the speed you want into factors.
concept.gears_c.seen: Mechanical watches, wind turbines, a tower clock
concept.cargo_a.name: Area and tiling
concept.cargo_a.idea: The crates' areas add up to the hold's area. Covering a space exactly with shapes is called tiling.
concept.cargo_a.seen: Packing a suitcase, laying floor tiles, loading a van
concept.cargo_b.name: Centre of mass
concept.cargo_b.idea: The ship sits level when the load's balance point is over the middle. That point is its centre of mass.
concept.cargo_b.seen: Carrying two shopping bags, loading a lorry, a tightrope walker's pole
concept.cargo_c.name: Packing with limits
concept.cargo_c.idea: You had to meet two rules at once: everything fits, and the weight balances. Problems like this are solved by narrowing the choices step by step.
concept.cargo_c.seen: Container ships, loading aircraft, arranging furniture
